title: Ad libitum meal energy intake is positively influenced by energy density, eating rate and hyper-palatable food across four dietary patterns
authors: Fazzino TL, Courville AB, Guo J, Hall KD
population: 2,733 ad libitum meals from four diets: ultra-processed, unprocessed, minimally processed low-fat and minimally processed low-carbohydrate
funder: This work was supported by the Intramural Research Program of the National Institutes of Health, National Institute of Diabetes & Digestive & Kidney Diseases.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing interests.
result: Meal-level analysis of energy density, hyper-palatability, protein content and eating rate. Energy density, eating rate and hyper-palatable foods were consistently positively related to meal energy intake across all four diets; protein content was positively related to meal energy intake during the ultra-processed and unprocessed diets only. Only the abstract, data statement and funding statement were read; effect sizes are in the paywalled full text.
